description.narrative:
Increased access to finance for MSMEs and WMSMEs and youth: Through the Project, IFC expects to support Khan Bank in further growing its financing to MSMEs and WMSMEs. The use of proceeds will be 100% MSMEs, of which (i) up to US$40 million will be earmarked exclusively for on-lending to WMSMEs, (ii) up to US$20 million will be earmarked for on-lending to MSMEs operated by young entrepreneurs, and (iii) up to US$15 million will be earmarked for on-lending to rural MSMEs.
Increased access to finance for agriculture: In Mongolia, limited access to finance remains a major constraint for the growth and modernization of the agricultural sector. The lack of medium- and long-term financing continues to hinder agro-enterprises from investing in productivity and value addition. Through the proposed investment, US$15 million will be earmarked for on-lending to agricultural MSMEs.
Competitiveness: Through this transaction, IFC aims to strengthen the competitiveness of Mongolias MSME sector, a key driver of economic diversification and job creation. IFCs support will also enable Khan Bank to expand into new asset classes and increase lending to youth entrepreneurs and agricultural businesses.

The project involves (1) up to US$130 million investment in Khan Bank JSC (Khan Bank or the Bank) for IFCs own account, consisting of (i) a 5-year USD-denominated senior loan of up to US$80 million; (ii) a 3-year USD-denominated senior loan, of up to US$20 million; and (iii) a Mongolian Tugrik (MNT)-linked loan of up to US$30 million equivalent, with a tenor of up to 5 years with the option to reset the rate at year 3, and (2) a 3-year USD-denominated senior syndicated loan of up to US$150 million to the Bank (the Project). The Project is intended to support the expansion of the Banks lending program for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Mongolia with carve-outs to women-owned/led MSMEs, rural MSMEs, MSMEs operated by young entrepreneurs, and agricultural MSMEs. In addition, IFC will provide a package of cross-currency swaps for the borrower to hedge up to US$300 million in FX exposure stemming from the USD loans.
